evidence: Dimension weights: task tests/scoring.toml is byte-for-byte the template/profile policy ([gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05), matching SKILL.md delivery profile and the Internal sheet note (functional 60 percent). Max non-functional contribution is 0.4 (< functional 0.6); gates carry no mass. score.py (identical to template) computes sum(w*score)/sum(w) and zeroes reward unless gates and floors pass (lines 41-48). Per-criterion weights: functional/judge.toml line 23 documents the scheme 'each criterion ... carries the sum of its legs' weights (1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief), 61 in all'; recomputed sum of the 12 weights 4.5+7+4+5.5+5+7+4+4.5+6+5.5+3.5+4.5 = 61.0, all multiples of 0.5 consistent with that scheme. Heaviest are hro_moves (7, single/stage moves, ordering, reject/reopen/undo of rejection, Hired refusal) and hro_undo_activity (7, multi-step undo safety plus full Activity audit), then hro_messaging (6) - the brief's two named product areas (pipeline board, conversations) and its explicit undo/all-or-none promises. Lightest are narrower bundles hro_unread_seen (3.5) and hro_two_people (4: stale-move 409-with-who plus 15 s live update), each still above any polish row's share. Normalised shares range 0.057-0.115 vs equal-weight 0.083 (max 1.4x deviation), so an equal-weight recompute (Colderwater lesson 2 audit) cannot swing the functional score far. Polish rows use the same documented scheme (polish/judge.toml comment): 2.0 for live-board preservation, live-thread draft/focus, earlier-messages place and sign-out draft resume (each stated in instruction.md paragraphs 3-4), 1.5 for failed-send handling (a professional default, not a brief headline) - lower weight for the less-explicit item is honest. Visual: five likert rows equal weight 1, documented. Gates: single binary criterion weight 1 under all_pass, no reward mass. No judge.toml carries a [judge] weight/model key. Weights are not used to steer the band: no odd single-criterion outlier, scheme documented in-file. Broken-app probe: an app that is styled nicely but functionally dead fails the render/constraints gates or the functional floor (needs >0.05, i.e. at least one passing functional criterion, smallest 3.5/61=0.057); even then polish rows are behavioural (live updates, failed-send recovery, session resume) so a dead app cannot farm them, leaving at most visual 0.2 + 0.6*0.057 ~ 0.23, below an app passing half the functional criteria with no polish (~0.30 + visual). Conforming-alternative probe: weights are attached to behaviours, not to implementation choices, so a conforming design (e.g. no drag, different layout) loses no weight-bearing credit through weighting. Observation (not a defect for this row): the per-leg classification behind each functional sum is not enumerated, so an auditor can confirm the totals and scheme but not each leg's 1.0/1.5/2.0 assignment; the floor value 0.05 means any single passing functional criterion clears it - that is template policy owned by row 43. No runtime reward-discrimination/ranking or model results exist (raw-evidence-index scope says so); this row's question is answerable statically, and the failed-vs-passed weight audit from lesson 2 cannot be performed until a model run exists - flagged for rows 42/43 and the owner, not a row-44 blocker.
